claims.statement: Metadata scopes this concept article to FPT, GHEC and GHES; titles and categories are navigation, not policy adoption.

GitHub creates a unique GITHUB_TOKEN for each workflow job. It is an installation token for the repository app, scoped to the repository containing the workflow; repository scope does not mean unrestricted privileges.

The token expires at job completion or its effective lifetime limit. Hosted jobs/token lifetime are bounded to six hours. A self-hosted job may run five days, but installation-token refresh is limited to twenty-four hours; longer jobs need another reviewed authentication method.
The job token is also available through github.token; an absent explicit secrets expression is not proof the job lacks this built-in credential.

The included trigger rule suppresses token-generated workflow events except workflow_dispatch/repository_dispatch and, where the feature applies, PR opened/synchronize/reopened events that create approval-required runs. A user with repository write access can approve those runs; other PR activity types do not run. This is not unconditional suppression.

For feature-enabled token-created or updated PRs, the article offers an App token or PAT when approval-free workflow triggering is required. This is an option needing least-privilege review, not authority to install an app or issue credentials.
The included rule says commits pushed by a workflow using GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger GitHub Pages builds. An observed push does not establish Pages execution.
Authentication and permissions links identify follow-up references; this reading does not certify those linked artifacts.
